entities.name: Raving cultists
entities.overview: Not all of the cults in The Dust are tied to the great battles that were once fought here. Some simply go mad as they try to gain the patronage of otherworldly entities they encounter among the many ruins. Blood stench rituals: In the Tracking Phase, roll 1D6. Roll an additional D6 for every warband member that became a casualty during the round. For every 5+, a Wracked (from this encounter list) is placed randomly along a battlefield edge. Trait: Poison (melee attacks only).

entities.name: Wind-swept to
entities.overview: The Dust itself. When their droning chant becomes one with the howling of the wind, the gates open. Conjuring chant: Every Tracking Phase, roll 1D6 per Wind-swept Wanderer on the table. Tally up any 6s rolled. Once a total of five 6s have been rolled, a randomly selected Aberration is placed randomly along a battlefield edge. Only one Aberration can be summoned per battle. Trait: Sand Dweller.

entities.name: Villainous hunting beasts raiders
entities.overview: The Dust is as wild a land as any border region, and raiders looking for pillage are common. Trait: Sand Dweller.

entities.name: Hunters of the
entities.overview: Sands Fierce and fast predators, these long-limbed beasts like to wear down their prey before the final pounce. Hard to target: Ranged attacks from a distance exceeding 6" will hit only on a natural 6 when targeting a Hunter of the Sands. This ability does not extend to any characters accompanying the Hunters. Ambush tactics: When playing a meeting engagement, after both sides have set up, roll 1D6 for each Hunter of the Sands. On a 5-6 the figure immediately moves into / directly behind the closest terrain feature to their front, then rolls again. This can happen multiple times. If no features remain between the Hunter and the closest warband member, move the figure to within 2" of the warband member and stop rolling for this Hunter. Trait: Sand Dweller.

entities.name: Secretive smugglers
entities.overview: While the common folk rarely find fault with smugglers, the authorities assuredly do. Ill-gotten gains: When setting up, roll 1D6 for each Smuggler who is not a Leader. On a 6 they are carrying goods. They get the Hang Back trait. If slain, they drop 1 Gold Mark worth of goods where they died which can be collected by moving to the location. If the battle ends, any goods not collected are lost.

entities.name: Highway robbers
entities.overview: These charlatans are often considered dashing characters, but most would cut your throat as soon as steal your jewelry. Your money or your life: You may pay them 2 Gold Marks to avoid the battle at any time.

entities.name: Cold-hearted poachers
entities.overview: Some poachers turn to hunting for more exciting prey than the deer of the Duke's forest.

entities.name: Knife-wielding thieves
entities.overview: The line between thievery and assassination can be quite narrow.

fields.value: Outflank. Deadly knives: Each enemy phase, the two thieves closest to your warband will throw knives instead of attacking in melee. Thieves cannot run out of ammunition and which thieves throw knives can change from round to round.

entities.name: Devout knives
entities.overview: Occasionally groups of malcontents elevate their random acts of brutality into a spiritual experience.

fields.value: Counter Attack. Blood-soaked faith: Every time a murderer knocks out a warband member, the enemy may ignore the next two Morale dice.

entities.overview: Fast Actions Phase, randomly pick a zealot that will pray this turn. In the Enemy Actions Phase, roll a D6: On a 6, the prayers are heard, and they unleash a magical bolt: This has a range of 8" and hits the closest foe with +2 / +2 damage. A survivor is knocked back 3". On any other result, the prayer goes unanswered. In all cases the zealot praying cannot move or take any other actions. The prayer is only interrupted by killing the zealot first.

entities.overview: The biggest qualification to joining the gang is a glorious lack of sophistication. Heavy strikes: When a Brute Stuns an opponent, they lose the ability to Parry or Counter Attack for the rest of that melee, regardless of the source of the ability.

entities.name: Repentant deserters
entities.overview: Some deserters want to reclaim their honor in a manner of speaking and take to harassing servants of the authorities. Well-supplied: Deserter archers do not run out of ammunition. Wanted men: Earn 1 Adventure Point for Holding the Field. Found wanting: Deserters do not benefit from the Courage in Numbers rule.
